topic: distributed constraint optimization; multi-agent reinforcement learning; coordination under partial observability
status: bounded cross-period synthesis from three directly relevant random-frame full texts; not a pooled effect; external replication/global novelty unresolved
claim: The audited DCOP and MARL papers do not show a universally best coordination mechanism. LP-DPOP-facts wins on some larger/harder random-graph cases but loses in particular domain-size, density, tightness, and smart-grid regimes; TeamReg/CoachReg gains vary by task, with TeamReg reversing sharply on adversarial COMPROMISE and parameter sharing leading on symmetric CHASE; PAC is strongest on some selected difficult SMAC maps but its own paper limits comparability across StarCraft II versions and leaves convergence/role specialization unresolved. The bounded signal is that an explicit coordination prior can help when it matches task structure, but the same prior can fail when constraints or incentives change.

sources.title: PAC: Assisted Value Factorisation with Counterfactual Predictions in Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning
locators: §5.2 footnote on SC2.4.10 and baseline provenance

interpretation: The sources concern different formalisms and are not head-to-head: distributed constraint optimization, continuous-control policy regularization, and partially observed StarCraft MARL. The shared task-conditional pattern is a research hypothesis, not a common mechanism or literature-wide estimate. LP-DPOP is body-dated 2013 with a 2014 arXiv version, so arXiv period is not first-publication chronology.
falsifiable_question: Under matched compute and tuning budgets, do the relative rankings of no coordination, action-predictability regularization, synchronized sub-policy selection, counterfactual joint-action assistance, and constraint-aware solver selection reverse systematically across preregistered cooperative/mixed-motive, symmetric/role-specialized, sparse/shaped-reward, and low/high-constraint-density strata?
primary_outcome: Per-task success/utility and failure rate across held-out task families, with compute/tuning cost and environment version fixed and documented; publish full stratum-level outcomes rather than only pooled means.
counterevidence_and_caveats: LP-DPOP-facts has strong wins at |X|=15/20 but loses at low p1 and p2=.4, solves only 60% at d=12, and underperforms in the tested smart-grid cases.
TeamReg improves SPREAD/BOUNCE but underperforms on adversarial COMPROMISE; CoachReg does not share that same reversal, and parameter sharing is best on CHASE.
PAC reports strong results on chosen hard SMAC maps, so the evidence is not uniformly negative; easy maps show closer performance.
Results cannot be pooled across distinct tasks, metrics, years, or implementations; the studies have no shared benchmark or independent replication in this audit.
suggested_design: Preregister a shared multi-agent suite with task strata for cooperative versus mixed motive, symmetry versus role specialization, sparse versus shaped reward, and low/high constraint density. Compare coordination interventions only where mathematically applicable, under common compute/tuning budgets and fixed software/environment versions, then evaluate held-out task families and report every cell. Separately probe DCOP solver-selection rules on unseen constraint graphs.

topic: human-agent collaboration; evolving requirements; long-horizon agent memory; retrieval-screen precision
status: single 2026 full-text audit; strong benchmark result but external validity unresolved
claim: GitHarness reports beating native cross-turn execution in all 30 model×harness×domain settings and matching or beating the strongest baseline in 28/30, but those seven-turn requirement trajectories are synthetic transformations of public benchmark tasks, not real user sessions. It also measures one assistant adapting to a user's changing requirements, not autonomous multi-agent coordination. Therefore the paper motivates real longitudinal evaluation of requirement tracking and local updates, but cannot validate either deployment performance with real users or progress in agent-agent coordination.

sources.title: GitHarness: Git Init Your Harness Working Memory for Perpetual User Requirements
locators: §5 Table 1: five domains × two backbones × three harnesses
§6 limitations on ambiguous/conflicting feedback and preservation
AI-use statement and ethics statement: synthetic benchmark trajectories; no real-user data

interpretation: This is an adjacent-topic screen false positive, not evidence against GitHarness's reported benchmark results. The paper's results remain meaningful for its synthetic protocol; generalization to authentic user feedback is untested.
falsifiable_question: On consented, de-identified longitudinal human-agent work sessions with requirement additions, edits, and withdrawals, does a versioned requirement/work-state system improve exact active-requirement fidelity and preserve unaffected verified artifacts over native history, summarization, and full restart, without increasing stale-content retention or regressions?
primary_outcome: Blindly adjudicated requirement fidelity, stale requirement carry-over, correctness of preserved unaffected artifacts, regressions outside edited dependency regions, clarification rate, task completion, and token/tool cost per requirement transition.
counterevidence_and_caveats: The reported benchmark gain is broad within its 30 tested combinations; it should not be dismissed merely because traces are synthetic.
Authors explicitly note ambiguous/conflicting feedback, state selection errors, and incomplete preservation remain difficult.
No user conversations or private data were included; no real-user external-validity evidence is available.
This work is human-agent requirement tracking, not autonomous multi-agent coordination.
suggested_design: Run a preregistered longitudinal study with consented/de-identified sessions; create immutable transition logs and verifiable artifact tests; compare versioned state against full transcript, summarization/retrieval, and restart; have blinded assessors measure stale carry-over, unaffected-work regressions, requirement fidelity, and resource cost. Keep this distinct from autonomous multi-agent benchmarks.

topic: multi-agent reinforcement learning; benchmark validity; partial observability; sparse-reward coordination
status: independent comparative follow-up across 25 tasks; not a direct replication of TeamReg/PAC; global novelty unresolved
claim: A separate nine-algorithm comparison over 25 cooperative tasks supports task-conditional rather than universal MARL rankings: centralized critics help on coordination-heavy partially observable tasks, while independent learners can compete on fully observable tasks; in sparse-reward Multi-Robot Warehouse, MAA2C/MAPPO improve over independent variants but COMA/VDN/QMIX show little or no learning. The benchmark further reports algorithm/rank sensitivity to parameter sharing, environment family, and implementation details. Thus “centralized training” or “value factorization” alone is not a reliable predictor of performance.

sources.title: Benchmarking Multi-Agent Deep Reinforcement Learning Algorithms in Cooperative Tasks
locators: §4 protocol: hyperparameter tuning, five seeds, CPU-hour budget

interpretation: This is an independent broad benchmark follow-up, but neither TeamReg nor PAC is among its nine algorithms. It strengthens the case for careful stratification; it does not directly confirm or refute those two methods. Hyperparameters are tuned on one task per environment and results use five seeds, so uncertainty and transfer across task configurations remain.
falsifiable_question: Across preregistered held-out cooperative tasks, does the effect of centralized critic access, value factorization, parameter sharing, and explicit coordination regularization interact reproducibly with observability, reward density, and agent heterogeneity under matched implementation and tuning budgets?
primary_outcome: For every task and algorithm report mean/median normalized return, success/failure probability, uncertainty across at least 10 seeds, training samples, wall-clock/compute, tuned configuration, parameter-sharing policy, and fixed code/environment versions; test rankings on task configurations not used for tuning.
counterevidence_and_caveats: Centralized critics improve some partial-observability/coordination regimes, so the benchmark does not imply centralized training is ineffective.

Simple independent methods remain competitive in some regimes, and certain value-decomposition methods fail in sparse-reward RWARE; this is task-dependent counterevidence to broad method-class claims.
Parameter-sharing average improvements are not clearly statistically significant in the paper and have environment-specific exceptions.
This 2021 benchmark is not a direct replication of TeamReg or PAC.
suggested_design: Preregister a factorial suite varying observability, reward density, agent count/heterogeneity, and cooperation structure. Use at least 10 seeds, tune on a disjoint task configuration, pin implementation/environment versions, and report per-cell results. Include simple independent baselines, CTDE, value factorization, and explicit coordination methods; treat methods with incompatible action spaces as separate blocks.
